No use, distribution or reproduction is permitted which does not comply with these terms. Severe COVID-19 is associated with profound lymphopenia and an elevated neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio. We applied a novel dimer avoidance multiplexed polymerase chain reaction next-generation sequencing assay to analyze T (TCR) and B cell receptor (BCR) repertoires. Surprisingly, TCR repertoires were markedly diminished during the early onset of severe disease but recovered during the convalescent stage. Monitoring TCR repertoires could serve as an indicative biomarker to predict disease progression and recovery. Panoramic concurrent assessment of BCR repertoires demonstrated isotype switching and a transient but dramatic early IgA expansion. Dominant B cell clonal expansion with decreased diversity occurred following recovery from infection. Profound changes in T cell homeostasis raise critical questions about the early events in COVID-19 infection and demonstrate that immune repertoire analysis is a promising method for evaluating emergent host immunity to SARS-CoV-2 viral infection, with great implications for assessing vaccination and other immunological therapies. COVID-19 SARS-CoV-2 T cell receptor B cell receptor immune repertoire biomarker National Natural Science Foundation of China-Yunnan Joint Fund 10.13039/501100011002 82041014, 81661148056 Introduction The current outbreak of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) was first reported in Wuhan, China ( 1 , 2 ). The virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is a virus closely related to SARS-CoV, endemic in 2003 ( 3 ). The virus caused low respiratory tract pneumonia, but it also affects multiple organs such as the kidney, liver, brain, gastrointestinal tract, and heart. The virus spreads by respiratory droplets, urine, and feces ( 4 , 5 ). Clinical symptoms of SARS-CoV-2 include fever, cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. The pneumonia in those with this disease is characterized by bilateral ground-glass opacities identified on chest CT scans ( 4 , 5 ). The majority of COVID-19 patients show mild or moderate symptoms and recover after proper clinical care. However, some COVID-19 patients rapidly develop severe pneumonia, subsequent multi-organ failure, and death ( 6 ). Pathologic examination reveals diffuse alveolar damage, proteinaceous plugs, and a prominent myeloid infiltrate and a paucity of lymphocytes ( 7 – 10 ). Despite global pandemic threats of COVID-19 disease, the host immune response against SARS-CoV-2 infection remains poorly understood. Lymphopenia is common in SARS-CoV-2 infected patients and was found as well as in SARS-CoV and Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) patients ( 4 , 6 , 11 ). It has been observed that the counts of total T cells, CD4+ and CD8+ subtype T cells, were dramatically reduced in severe COVID-19 cases with increased expression of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1) and T cell immunoglobulin mucin 3 (Tim-3), indicating activation and T cell exhaustion ( 12 ). Monitoring the dynamics of lymphocyte number and phenotype has been suggested as a means to predict the severity of COVID-19 ( 13 ). Older COVID-19 patients with comorbidities are at a particularly high risk of severe pneumonia and death. The diminished T cell repertoire and progressive defects in T cell and B cell function in older patients could limit viral clearance and prolong the innate proinflammatory response ( 14 , 15 ). The human adaptive immune system consists of both naïve and memory cells, which express either cell surface B cell receptors (BCRs) or T cells receptors (TCRs), in aggregate termed the adaptome ( 16 ). Recently, next-generation sequencing (NGS) of BCRs and TCRs have been used widely to evaluate immunity ( 17 – 21 ). Analyzing the full repertoires could provide a better understanding of the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 and other infections. Because all seven of the immune repertoire chains, including IgH (all isotypes), IgK, IgL, TCR-Alpha, Beta chains, and TCR – Gamma, Delta chains are amplified under the same conditions in one PCR reaction with our method, the expression level of these genes can be directly compared with an inclusive and quantitative pattern ( 16 ). Here, we deeply investigated the peripheral blood repertoire from patients throughout their course of COVID-19 disease, demonstrating dynamic changes over the disease course.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: SARS-CoV-2 infection leads to profound lymphopenia, characterized by diminished T lymphocytes and abnormal TRA/TRB expression, implying T cells undergo acute apoptotic events or egress from circulation, potentially due to virus-induced epithelial destruction and increased vascular permeability leading to nonselective leakage into the lung. T cells are crucial for virus clearance and antibody-mediated protection, as evidenced by persistence of MERS-CoV in T cell-deficient mice. Decreased CD8+ T cells in COVID-19 patients are associated with markers of activation and exhaustion. The immune response includes an early IgM to IgG isotype switch and a transient, dramatic IgA surge, with IgM-expressing B cells mobilized first, followed by T cell-mediated class-switch. The early activation and increase of IgA-expressing B cells in peripheral blood may bypass normal T cell controls, potentially utilizing innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) in the lung. Aberrant IgK/IgL ratios suggest strong B cell selection events, especially around days 8-15 post-symptom onset, with dominant clonal expansion of IgH/IgK/IgL chains observed around two weeks post-infection. Persistent affinity maturation of virus-specific antibodies (IgG) occurs within the germinal center, and the mobilization of IgM/IgG/IgA is hypothesized to prevent viral-induced pathology. Profound changes in T cell homeostasis occur during early COVID-19 infection.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: TCR repertoires exhibited dynamic changes across the disease course, being markedly diminished in early severe COVID-19 (days 4-7 in moderate and severe cases) but recovering during convalescence (D17-22), with TRB expression reaching healthy levels. Severe COVID-19 is characterized by profound lymphopenia, an elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and dramatically reduced T cell subsets (Total T cells, CD4+, CD8+). B cell repertoires also showed dynamic shifts: IgH and IgL proportions rapidly increased early (D4-7) and remained high, while IgK showed a slower increase, peaked in mid-stage (D8-15), and then dropped (D17-22). IgM-expressing B cells were significantly lower in early COVID-19, whereas IgG expression increased early and peaked in mid-stages, persisting for over six months post-clearance. A significant transient IgA surge was observed in early infection (D4-7), followed by a decrease (D8-15). In severe ICU patients, IgH/IgK/IgL chains were largely dominant, with dramatically reduced TRB and lower IgK diversity, indicating distinct immune profiles based on disease severity and stage. The expression of TCRs dramatically decreased during the early stage of infection (days 4–7) in both moderate and severe COVID-19 cases, indicating a similar initial immune response pattern irrespective of disease intensity.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Lymphopenia is a common feature in SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS patients, suggesting it is not exclusive to SARS-CoV-2 among these viral infections. However, the specific dynamic changes observed in TCR and BCR repertoires, including TRB, IgH/IgK/IgL proportions, and their return to normal levels, are indicative of SARS-CoV-2 infection progression and recovery, distinguishing them from stable repertoires in healthy influenza vaccinees. The rapid and distinct predominance of B cells expressing IgA very early following SARS-CoV-2 infection is reported as the first such finding, suggesting a specific IgA response unique to this novel virus. Aberrant IgK/IgL ratios indicate selection events specific to COVID-19 infection, particularly during days 8-15 post-symptom onset. The changes in immune repertoire were observed in COVID-19 patients but not in the healthy seasonal influenza vaccinee control.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: COVID-19 patients (including moderate and severe cases, older patients with comorbidities), healthy donors, and a healthy seasonal influenza vaccinee used as controls.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Monitoring TCR repertoires, particularly TRB expression, can serve as a critical indicative biomarker to predict disease progression and recovery from SARS-CoV-2 infection. Immune repertoire analysis offers a promising method for evaluating host immunity to SARS-CoV-2, with significant implications for assessing vaccination efficacy and other immunological therapies. In older patients with comorbidities, diminished T cell repertoire and impaired T/B cell function can limit viral clearance, prolong proinflammatory responses, and increase the risk of severe pneumonia and multi-organ failure. The dynamic changes in TCR and BCR repertoires provide a holistic understanding of COVID-19, enabling close immunity monitoring. Decreased CD8+ T cells, associated with activation and exhaustion markers, serve as an early indicator for potential ICU treatment. Rapid diagnosis can be aided by measuring SARS-CoV-2-specific IgM antibodies, while isolation of IgA-specific antibodies is important for early diagnosis and therapeutic development. The increasing percentage of IgA expressing B cells indicates IgA may be synthesized and widely migrate to mucosal sites (respiratory/gastrointestinal tract) to play an early immune function to clear the virus. Global and longitudinal analyses of adaptive immunity in COVID-19 patients can provide insights into virus infection mechanisms, assist in clinical treatment assessment, and aid in the development of antiviral therapeutics and vaccines. The evolving immune system's response to SARS-COV-2 infection provides valuable insights into the disease's natural history, host response, and effective clinical treatment. Clonally expanded IgH sequences during infection may be a source for developing neutralizing antibodies. Aberrant IgK/IgL ratios and dominant clonal expansion around two weeks after infection suggest significant B cell selection events.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Diagnostic/Prognostic Utility: TCR and BCR repertoire dynamics (e.g., TRB expression, TRA/TRB recovery, IgH/IgK/IgL changes, low unique TCR reads) are valuable for assessing disease stage, progression, and recovery. SARS-CoV-2-specific IgM antibody measurement facilitates rapid diagnosis, and IgA-specific antibodies are important for early diagnosis and therapy. Adverse Risk: Decreased CD8+ T cells is an early indicator for requiring ICU treatment. Older patients with comorbidities are at high risk of severe outcomes due to immune defects. Protective Benefit: Mobilization of IgM/IgG/IgA is associated with preventing viral-induced pathology, and increased IgA expression suggests an early immune function to clear the virus.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The study highlights TCR repertoires, specifically TRA and TRB expression, as reliable 'reference indicators of disease recovery' for SARS-CoV-2 infection. The use of a novel dimer avoidance multiplexed PCR next-generation sequencing (DAM-PCR/NGS) assay, incorporating UMIs, enhances accuracy and provides a comprehensive, quantitative view of all seven immune repertoire chains, making it a promising method for evaluating host immunity. Aberrant IgK/IgL ratios, previously observed in other B cell diseases, lend external consistency to their significance in COVID-19 selection events. SARS-CoV-2-specific IgM antibody measurement is reliable for rapid diagnosis, and IgA-specific antibody isolation holds potential for early diagnosis and therapy. The comprehensive DAM-PCR/NGS method offers a 'panoramic view of repertoire dynamics'. However, limitations include the inability to validate TCR/BCR frequency dynamics with lymphocyte counts, CRP, or sera titers; absence of pre-infection repertoires; reliance on peripheral blood samples (representing a small fraction of total circulation); and lack of examination of SARS-CoV-2 specific TCR/BCR repertoires.
recommended_alternatives: Monitoring the dynamics of lymphocyte number and phenotype.
Further studies are needed to elaborate the mechanism of the aberrant IgK/IgL finding.
Studies on clonally expanded IgH sequences may be used as a source for developing neutralizing antibodies.
Single-cell PCR of SARS-CoV-2-specific B cells combined with BCR repertoire analysis for accelerating identification and cloning of neutralizing antibodies.
Integrated analysis of repertoire sequencing and single-cell transcriptomics, alongside antibody cloning, for a comprehensive explanation of adaptive immune response against virus infection.
Further studies to clarify if T cells are present in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from the lungs of severe patients and in lungs of people with mild infections in the early stage of infection.
Further studies to expand the repertoire dynamics of T/B cell subsets to give insight into why lymphopenia occurs.
Longitudinal analysis of B cells expressing each of the individual IgH, Igκ and Igλ chains for a holistic view of antibody repertoire changes over time.
